page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-32 is a graphics- and compute-accelerated virtual machine within the GPU Machines family. The configuration is provisioned with 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, featuring two threads per core and 38 MB of shared L3 cache. It includes 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, carrying 24 GB of VRAM. This server type includes zero local disk storage and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage and external IP provisioning for network-attached workflows.

Benchmark measurements indicate specialized acceleration characteristics alongside balanced general compute throughput. The NVIDIA L4 accelerator registers top-tier inference speeds for smaller and mid-sized language models, processing 11,863 tokens per second on prompt intake for 135M parameter models and 52.67 generation tokens per second on 7B models. Throughput reduces to average tier tiers when processing 70B models, constrained by the single GPU footprint and memory capacity. System compute performance reflects average multi-threaded capacity, scoring 24,012.33 in PassMark CPU and 9,347.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, whereas single-core performance scores in the bottom quartile due to conservative clock scaling.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-32 offers a dense allocation of 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB RAM paired with an enterprise L4 accelerator, avoiding the overhead of larger multi-GPU server designs. The main tradeoff is the absence of bundled local NVMe storage and subdued single-threaded performance, making the system less suited for high-frequency trading or single-core compile bottlenecks. The machine profile fits real-time AI inference pipelines, video rendering, computer vision, static web serving clusters, and containerized GPU-accelerated microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-32 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine powered by 32 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, 128 GB of system RAM, and one NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. The system features a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation but includes no local storage or default public IPv4 addressing. Synthetic benchmarks place single-core execution in the lower quartile, whereas multi-core throughput and memory operations sit in the mid-range. The Ada Lovelace GPU delivers top-tier performance for small- to mid-scale large language model inference workloads, sustaining high prompt and text generation rates on models up to 7B parameters. The instance represents an efficient consolidation of balanced host memory, dedicated host threads, and entry enterprise acceleration, making it well-suited for AI model inference serving, graphics transcoding, media processing, and visual computing pipelines.
og_description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-32 features an NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB VRAM, 32 Intel Xeon vCPUs, and 128 GB RAM. The instance lacks local storage and delivers top-tier throughput for small to medium LLM inference.
